<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD defines sources for different architectures that point to prebuilt release binaries hosted on GitHub. The `source` array entries use a standard format, downloading tarballs from the project's official release page using HTTPS. The URLs are constructed using a predefined `_relurl` variable, which points to a tagged release on the maintainer's GitHub repository. There is no command substitution, obfuscated code, or remote execution during the sourcing of the PKGBUILD.

The `pkgver` is hardcoded and does not involve any dynamic fetching or evaluation from external sources. The top-level scope contains only safe variable assignments and array definitions. Checksums are provided and not set to 'SKIP', so sources will be verified after download. Even if they were skipped, that would not make this phase unsafe, as verification is a separate step. No functions (`prepare`, `build`, etc.) are executed due to `--noprepare` and `--nobuild`, and no malicious side effects occur during sourcing.

The package follows standard AUR practices: it fetches prebuilt binaries from an expected upstream source, and no data exfiltration, dynamic code evaluation, or unauthorized network activity occurs during the `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` and `makepkg --printsrcinfo` phases.
</details>
<summary>
No dangerous code executes during source fetch
</summary>
</security_assessment>
